etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English badly, baddely, baddeliche, equivalent to bad +‎ -ly.

Things are going badly for her: she did badly in her exams owing to a badly designed studying schedule.

definitions.definition: Very much; to a great degree.

quote.citation: 2008, Darl Larsen, Monty Python's Flying Circus, page 276:
quote.text: In late 1970, Labour assumed the shadow posts, having lost badly (and unforeseenly) in the summer General Election.
